Manila Mayor @IskoMoreno has ordered the filing of criminal and civil charges against Jelsie Construction and Supply after the company allegedly demolished the Rizal Avenue Sports Athletics Complex (RASAC) covered court in Sta. Cruz without any permits.

During a press briefing at Bulwagan ng Maynila, Moreno said the demolition and ongoing construction of the “Centro Comunidad de Santa Cruz” project pushed through without coordination with the local government or the required building and demolition permits.

“The property demolished is valued at ₱10.4 million and has long served as an evacuation center, a police outpost, a daycare center, and even a pandemic isolation site,” Moreno said, stressing that the facility’s destruction deprived residents of a vital public space.

Moreno outlined three sets of criminal complaints to be lodged before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office:

- Malicious Mischief (Article 328, Revised Penal Code): for damages caused to RASAC facilities.

- Unlawful Demolition and Construction: for violating the National Building Code by proceeding without a demolition or building permit.

- Violation of the Risk Reduction and Preparedness Equipment Protection Act: for tearing down a government facility used for disaster response and humanitarian purposes.

A separate civil case will also be pursued, with the city government issuing a demand letter against Jelsie Construction. Moreno presented certifications from the City Accountant and the Office of the Building Official confirming that no permits were granted for the project.

“Walang demolition permit, walang building permit. Sinira ang property na pag-aari ng taong bayan sa lungsod ng Maynila ng walang kaukulang permiso,” Moreno declared.

The mayor further tied Jelsie Construction to the ongoing controversy surrounding questionable flood control projects, citing national government records and previous remarks by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

From 2022 to 2025, Moreno said, Manila saw ₱14.3 billion allocated to flood control works, much of it awarded to a small circle of favored contractors — including Jelsie Construction. Despite this, flooding in the capital remains widespread.

“Bumaha ng pondo sa Maynila, bumaha pa rin sa Maynila,” Moreno said.

He added that at least 112 ongoing projects have been operating without permits or paying contractor’s taxes to the city.

Moreno vowed to pursue cases against all contractors found disregarding local and national laws.

“Welcome kayong magnegosyo sa Maynila, but you must follow simple procedure. Walang holy cow,” he warned, making clear that no company will be exempt from accountability.

Some persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) at the Negros Occidental District Jail (NODJ) in Barangay Tabunan, Bago City held a noise barrage on Thursday morning, calling to oust its jail warden Jail Chief Insp. Crisyrel Awe due to alleged unfair treatment inside the facility.

Jail Senior Insp. Juniven Umadhay, spokesperson of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology-Negros Island Region (BJMP-NIR), said the protest action came days after the “gun-throwing” incident inside the facility on Sunday, August 24, which prompted the jail to implement stringent measures for the safety of the personnel and PDLs.

Umadhay said that there was no maltreatment or abuse among the PDLS inside the facility, as heightened security measures have been imposed since last month after an attempt on the life of a jail officer outside the facility.

The Police Regional Office-Negros Island Region (PRO-NIR) has deployed personnel upon the request of the jail for security assistance.|via Glazyl Masculino

📷 PRO-NIR

Hinamon ni Manila 6th District Rep. Benny Abante si Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte na “patunayan” ang sinabi nitong “PR stunt” lang ang imbestigasyon ng gobyerno sa anomalya sa flood control projects sa bansa.

Untag pa ni Abante kay Mayor Baste, kung pondo sa flood control projects lang din ang pag-uusapan, bakit hindi raw usisain ng alkalde ang nakatatandang kapatid nitong si Davao City 1 District Rep. Paolo ‘Pulong’ Duterte tungkol sa sarili nitong pondo laban sa baha, na problema rin sa siyudad.

“Suggestion ko kay Mayor Baste, tanungin niya ‘yung kanyang kapatid na congressman. Magkano ba ang pondong nakuha ni Congressman Pulong nung congressman siya, nung panahon ng kanyang father?” tanong ni Abante, tinukoy si dating pangulong Rodrigo Duterte, na naging presidente ng bansa simula 2016 hanggang 2022.

Matatandaang kinumpirma mismo ni noon ay Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Undersecretary Maria Catalina Cabral na tumanggap ang distrito ni Congressman Pulong ng P13.7-billion infrastructure funds—kabilang ang para sa flood control projects—noong 2020, P25 bilyon noong 2021, at P13 bilyon noong 2022—o kabuuang P51.7 bilyon sa loob ng tatlong taon.

Isang bilyong piso lang ang pinakamalaking development funds na natatanggap ng bawat kongresista.

“I-reveal niya kung magkano, kung saan ginamit ‘yang pondong ‘yan, kung papaano ginamit ‘yan, kung ilang milyon ang napunta sa flood control projects, at kung bakit malaki pa ang baha sa Davao,” dagdag pa ni Abante.

“Kung talagang PR stunt ‘to, patunayan niya,” mensahe pa ni Abante kay Mayor Baste.
